chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris and others from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali from Amr ibn Saeed from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqa from Ammar al-Sabati from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who leads a group in prayer while they are in a place lower than his place where he is praying. He said: If the Imam is on something resembling a platform, or on a place higher than their place, their prayer is not valid; and if he is higher than them by the measure of a finger, or more, or less, when the elevation is by the belly of a wadi (ravine).

So if the land is flat, or if there is an elevation in a part of it, so the Imam stands in the elevated place and those behind him stand lower than him, and the ground is flat, except that they are in a sloping place, he said: There is no problem.
He said, and he was asked: If the Imam stands lower than the place of those who pray behind him? He said: There is no problem.

And he said: If a man is above a house or other than that, whether it is a shop or something else, and the Imam is praying on the ground lower than him, it is permissible for the man to pray behind him and follow his prayer, even if he is higher than him by a great amount.
ai.seo_question: What are the rules for the Imam's position relative to the followers in terms of height during congregational prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the fiqh of vertical alignment in congregational prayer, distinguishing between significant elevation (such as on a dukkan or platform) which may invalidate the prayer if the followers are on flat ground, and slight elevation or natural slopes which are permissible. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the physical continuity of the row (saff) and the Imam's visibility, ensuring the prayer remains valid even when the terrain is uneven or the Imam is positioned lower than the followers.
